doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Singing fast on Cloudburst and his law and English studies
summary: His English major and law studies gave him command of words, and the speed vanished once he sang it.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. It goes by so fast. But every time I hear it I go, how did you do that? How did you do that? Did they record you at 33 and then press it at 78 or something? I mean it’s just © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -9-

Well I think I should tell you, I actually studied law. My major was English, my minor was history, and I was a law student. And I had 18 months to get my law degree. And I got the only A in speech class in four years. And I got the only A in the creative writing class in seven years. And so I was a bit of a academic star you know for that, because the guy that wrote the book on creative writing, Dr. Milt Marks, was well known. I think he won a Pulitzer Prize and he’s well known at all university levels, especially in all the English departments. So I knew how to use words. And I knew all about that. But as far as speaking that fast, I would have said to myself, I have to slow this down. But I found that when I started to sing it, the speed aspect of it disappeared. I just sang it.
It’s a classic, I’ll tell you that.
Well, but that’s a very high praise. That’s high praise coming from you. I thank you very much for that. Because all it is is it’s fun to me. I love it.
